text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Nigeria's crude oil reserves including condensates put at 24 billion barrels by end of 1996.
- Two Nigerian pilgrims are among hundreds of Moslems killed in fire at haj camp in Saudi Arabia on Tuesday.
- Forty-four people were killed in ethnic clashes in the oil city of Warri in the midwest last Saturday, according to comunity leaders there.
- Tribunal orders that Afrobeat musician Fela Anikulapo-Kuti should be remanded at Kirikiri prison pending his formal arraignment on Monday on charges of possessing cannabis.
- Military ruler General Sani Abacha, other Nigerian leaders charge countrymen to extend love and kindness to one another as the country's Moslems mark eid-el-kabir.
- Manager of Products and Pipelines Marketing Company, which is responsible for fuel supplies, blames recent petrol shortage in the country on vandalisation of the company's pipelines.
- United States ambassador Walter Carrington says frosty relations between his country and Nigeria are unlikely to change soon.
- Federal government orders its agencies to carry out periodic parade of their staff in order to stamp out payment of salaries to ghost workers.
- Demand for foreign exchange at weekly auction rises to $71.164 million this week from $62 million last week.
